milestone: M41 External Mode Pack Trust Revocation

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds runtime-owned signer revocation state and makes approved candidate trust fail closed after a trusted signer is revoked.
Keeps revocation authorization and approval denial in Rust runtime instead of VSIX policy.
Persists bounded revocation evidence without deleting historical trust events or storing raw candidate/provenance data.
Gives scheduled callers deterministic revoke/replay behavior and prevents headless approval from consuming stale signer trust.

answers.strategic_capabilities: mode_pack_runtime with support from runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: modepack.revokeSigner records bounded signer revocation evidence, and modepack.approveCandidate treats a revoked trusted signer as not currently trusted before writing approval state.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M40.1 can add trusted signer policy, but trust is permanent; there is no runtime-owned way to revoke a compromised or retired signer.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A once-trusted signer remains able to authorize future external Mode Pack candidates indefinitely, so Brownie cannot recover from signer compromise.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M40.1 trust creation, M39.2 provenance-gated approval, and M39.1 provenance verification because it removes current trust without deleting historical trust evidence.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. Revocation is a new explicit state-changing policy mutation and cannot be represented by trustSigner, approveCandidate, or a summary wrapper.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds bounded mutation evidence only and no report, digest, history, readiness, preview, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The runtime records signer revocation and rejects approval when the verified provenance signer has a revocation snapshot.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers get replay-safe revocation and fail-closed approval behavior when trust has been withdrawn.
answers.milestone_progress: Completes the minimal M41 trust-revocation vertical slice by adding explicit revoke, replay, ledger evidence, and approval enforcement.

exit_criteria: modepack.revokeSigner records one bounded signer revocation entry with explicit authorization
signer revocation replay returns the existing revocation entry without duplicate ModePackSignerRevoked events
modepack.approveCandidate re-reads current revocation state for the verified provenance signer before writing approved state
approval rejects revoked signer policy without writing approved candidate state
revocation preserves historical ModePackSignerTrusted ledger evidence and records referenced trust handles
RPC and ledger payloads contain bounded metadata only and no raw candidate JSON, raw statement, raw signature bytes, or raw public key bytes
Behavior tests cover signer revocation mutation, revocation replay, authorization denial, bounded output, VSIX validation, and approval enforcement

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M41.1 changes signer revocation and approval behavior; review must confirm this is runtime trust revocation, not a wrapper surface.
